chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a slave who married without the permission of his master, so he said: 'That is up to his master; if he wishes, he validates it, and if he wishes, he separates them.' I said, 'May Allah keep you well! Al-Hakam ibn Uteybah, and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and their companions say that the origin of the marriage is invalid, and the master's validation is not permissible for him.' So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He did not disobey Allah; he only disobeyed his master. So when he validates it, it is valid for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's marriage if done without the master's permission?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'ajaz' (ratification) in slave marriages, contrasting the Imami view with the Hanafi-leaning opinion of Al-Hakam ibn 'Utainah and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that the marriage is fundamentally void. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the slave's act was a civil disobedience to his master rather than a religious transgression, allowing the master's subsequent approval to validate the union. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the status of slaves, prioritizing the master's authority over the intrinsic validity of the contract.
